reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical structure of RacketVision lies in its fusion of ball trajectory and racket pose through attention mechanisms. The ball trajectory prediction module maps a history of ball positions to a future sequence, incorporating either unimodal (ball-only) or multimodal (ball + racket) inputs. Cross-attention enables dynamic conditioning where the ball’s past trajectory serves as query and the racket pose as key-value pair. This is modeled as a learned mapping from history to future, with latent features derived from both modalities. The key insight is that concatenation of features leads to degradation in performance when the two modalities interact, whereas cross-attention preserves semantic alignment. In GSI, this translates to Bayesian event-conditioned inference where trajectory forecasts are updated based on observed racket poses. In GSE, it becomes a state-transition model where the next ball state depends on both prior motion and current racket configuration. The failure mode occurs when the model overfits to soft-labeled training data or lacks sufficient inter-frame consistency in sparse annotations. The breakdown regime is defined by low-racket visibility or mid-flight states where no interaction occurs, rendering fusion ineffective.
